title: Formal smoothness at a prime spreads to a smooth principal neighbourhood
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be prime, and suppose the localization $A_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is formally smooth over $R$ for the $0$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Then there exists $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $A_g$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Here $A_g$ denotes the ring of fractions with denominators in $\{1,g,g^2,\ldots\}$.
